prerequisites: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (2nd Year, 1st Semester). It is strongly recommended to have passed it.

learning_outcomes.text: Have knowledge and understanding of the theoretical foundations of electronic engineering and its practical applications.
Acquire a comprehensive awareness of the multidisciplinary context of electronics within the field of industrial engineering.

Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve electronic engineering problems and their main applications using established theoretical and practical methods, as well as basic design rules for their implementation.

Be able to design and conduct experiments for the characterization and application of simple electronic systems, as well as develop critical thinking for data interpretation and drawing conclusions regarding the correct functioning of these systems.
Know how to apply the technical skills acquired for the experimental analysis of electronic systems in an electronics laboratory.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve electronic engineering problems.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.

syllabus_topics: 1.2 Process of creating an electronic system.
1.4 Review of electrical circuit theorems we will need.
Topic 2. Electronic instrumentation. Sensors and transducers
2.1 Laboratory instrumentation and electronic signal measurements.
4.3 Introduction to power supply and energy conversion systems.
Topic 5. Digital subsystems and A/D and D/A conversion
5.1 Basics of digital electronics. Number systems.
5.2 Boolean algebra. Basic logic gates. Logic functions and representation.
5.4 A/D and D/A converters. Characteristic parameters.
Practical sessions addressing the fundamentals of analog and digital electronics. Use of electronic circuit measurement techniques.
teaching_methods: Exercise solving classes in small groups

Classes in small groups in laboratory and/or computer room fostering self-learning, self-construction of knowledge, and problem-based learning (PBL) in accordance with the EHEA methodology (European Higher Education Area)
Flipped classroom, using a SPOC (Small Private Online Course) for laboratory competencies

assessment_methods.method: Part 1 Evaluation (Partial or Final Exam Part 1)

assessment_rules: To qualify for continuous assessment, students must complete the practices and take the partial evaluation (Part 1). For students under continuous assessment, the final grade is the sum of Practices (4 points), Part 1 Evaluation (3 points, from partial or final exam part 1), and Part 2 Evaluation (3 points, from final exam part 2). A minimum of 4 points out of 10 is required in each of the two exam parts (Part 1 and Part 2). Penalties are applied to the final practice score if individual practice grades are low. If continuous assessment conditions are not met, the final grade is based solely on the final exam (Part 1 Evaluation + Part 2 Evaluation), with a minimum of 4 points required in each part.
